current_answer: The Plausible Community Edition announcement links to a self-hosted comparison page. In the 31 October 2026 crawler view, that page linked CE to its GitHub repository and separately labelled its prominent Cloud-trial button as a 30-day Plausible Cloud offer. A saved-link assertion and controlled fixture mutation distinguished the branches; no normal logged-out browser, redirect trace or conversion outcome was observed. Review the intended next action and exact CTA placement before promotion.

catalogue_card.question: Does a Plausible CE announcement lead to CE or Cloud?
catalogue_card.text: The comparison offers a CE repository link and a separate labelled Cloud trial. Saved crawler links only; live browser and outcomes unverified.

summary: Mautic and Activepieces CE are conditional choices for teams able to operate their platform or workflow layer.
n8n is a source-available/fair-code workflow and optional AI orchestration option; its Sustainable Use License is not OSI-style open source and may restrict commercial provision/hosting.
Marketing Agent OS is a portable harness library, not a marketing application. Its 25 September audit found a component-level provenance boundary and host-owned execution controls.
Loopmark is retained only under the direct label ‘exploratory local drafting CLI’. MarketingOS AI was examined but is not recommended or catalogued.
The research library contains dated dossiers and permanent report links for all completed research runs.
The 24 September operations guide distinguishes a local Mautic form/contact artifact from a local Activepieces CE run artifact and requires human review and teardown for either.

The 26 September Mautic 7.2.1 audit documents campaign, preference, queue, cron, role, and report surfaces while separating them from operator-owned consent, delivery, approval, monitoring, and recovery work.

The 27 September Activepieces CE audit documents the manual/local draft path, paid governance boundary, in-flight retry risk, encryption-key and multi-store recovery duties, and conflicting retention/log-cap documentation.
The 28 September synthesis assigns draft, exact-version human decision, optional CE run, sender/CRM action evidence, consent and recovery to distinct owners; no combined integration was tested.

The 29 September small-list audit keeps an existing operated sender as the first conditional option, Keila as a private-evaluation candidate only, and Listmonk as a list/campaign tool without an established built-in welcome trigger. Neither is added to the vetted four-layer shortlist.

The 30 September Keila v0.30.3 source follow-up read tagged README/build files and a registry digest listing. K1 partly advanced but remains open; K3 and X1 remain open. No image inspection, restore or send occurred, and no shortlist addition was made.

The 1 October Listmonk v6.2.0 tagged-path audit found no distinct native welcome in inspected DOI confirmation, core hook, template, campaign and transactional paths. A reviewed external trigger/ledger or manual action is required; /api/tx does not enforce consent or dedupe. No runtime test or shortlist addition.

The 2 October Listmonk v6.2.0 private DOI/suppression test did not run: pinned artifact, isolated runtime, local-only mail sink, egress proof and teardown were unavailable. A reproducible fictional-data test card was prepared; no observed behavior, send clearance or shortlist addition follows.

The 3 October phpList v3.6.16 audit found a tagged call to sendMail for one immediate page-keyed system confirmation message after DOI, not a delayed welcome sequence. Current docs describe editable global/page copy; exact-tag signup/editor fallback, suppression, duplicate and provider outcome remain untested. Conditional research entry only.

The 4 October small-list welcome decision contract separates DOI request, immediate welcome, ongoing campaign and delayed sequence. It puts the existing-sender evidence test first and maps consent, approval, suppression, attempt, provider outcome, duplicate hold and restore. No runtime, sink, provider or restore test occurred; no send clearance.

The 5 October Ghost v6.63.0 source audit found native member-signup welcome triggers and current help for free/paid welcome emails. Reuse is conditional on an already-operated publication site and a complete consent-to-recovery record; no install, send, provider or restore test occurred. Delayed sequences are an opt-in beta, not covered by the one-message finding.

The 6 October Marketing Agent OS one-skill installation test did not run. The intended pinned checkout was unreachable and a network-denied boundary could not be established. No skill or target was selected, no installer was executed, and no file effects were observed. No recommendation change.

The 7 October Postiz v2.25.0 audit separates unlisted preview comments from enforced client sign-off. Current docs explicitly disclaim a blocking approved flag; no-channel draft was not established. No instance, connection, provider action or security test occurred; Postiz is not shortlisted.

The 8 October Umami v3.4.0 tagged-source audit supports a synthetic post-click pilot: UTM-tagged page-view counts and a separate signup-confirmed signal. No site, newsletter, instance, goal report or browser fixture was tested; no verified account, ROI or shortlist claim.

The 9 October Plausible CE v3.2.1 tagged-source audit supports a conditional synthetic post-click pilot for generic newsletter UTMs, pageviews, a site-emitted signup-confirmed event and a goal rate. It does not verify delivery, an account or incremental effect. CE/Cloud, component licences, two-database operation and the /storybook patch boundary are explicit; no runtime test or shortlist addition.

The 10 October SiteOne v2.5.1 source audit makes manual five-route review the default. A crawler is conditional on explicit owner authorization and an external exact-scope guard; --url-list bypass and the ten-page noindex alert threshold are explicit. No crawl or runtime test occurred.

The 11 October YOURLS 1.10.6 tagged-source audit puts the direct approved URL with UTMs first. Private shortening needs separate approval, rollback and operations; 301 caching can limit retargeting and clicks do not prove outcomes. No runtime test or shortlist addition.

The 12 October promptfoo 0.124.1 source audit makes fact-card and human checklist the first route, a tiny script the recurring-rule route, and promptfoo a conditional matrix route. No eval or copy approval was performed.

The 13 October ResourceSpace source-only decision recommends folder/register and three-placement ledger for one image, compares a script and self-hosted DAM, and distinguishes expiry-field warnings from configured plugin/cron actions. No immutable 11.0 artifact, install or external replacement was tested.

The 14 October localized-offer audit places an approved English source card and bilingual six-placement register before Weblate. Each locale/placement needs an exact artifact, separate language and fact review, and destination receipt; email stop is unconfirmed in the fictional example. Weblate 2026.10.1 was assessed from release and versioned docs, not tagged code or runtime.

The 15 October calendar-to-receipt audit puts the existing calendar and versioned ledger first. A fictional three-channel exception shows delayed landing, ambiguous email cancellation and already-public social v1. Vikunja v2.7.0 tasks can coordinate follow-up, not prove external channel states. Tagged source and living help only; no runtime or campaign test.

The 16 October two-newsletter audit puts the existing ESP first. Listmonk v6.2.0 tagged campaign and import paths show disabled and single-opt-in unconfirmed are not generic no-send holds; overwrite collisions and late events demand row-level parity. Nine fictional contacts; no runtime migration, send or restore.

The 17 October form-to-contact audit puts the existing form and CRM route first. Mautic 7.2.1 docs describe submission and contact IDs, not a CRM receipt. No connector was run; 7.2 support status is unresolved due to conflicting project release-page signals.

The 18 October Mailpit v1.31.5 pre-send audit keeps a verified existing preview/test path first. Tagged source documents capture, default non-loopback listeners and optional relay/forwarding; no message was sent or captured. Provider and recipient outcomes remain untested.

The 19 October SerpBear v3.1.0 source audit starts with matched Search Console observed clicks/impressions. A fixed provider snapshot is conditional; page-versus-domain matching, depth and errors can explain disagreement. Fictional triage only; no live rank or restore test.

The 20 October page-refresh diagnosis uses a fictional three-page card and exact Search Console cuts: refresh only after a relevant sustained loss and independently verified content gap; diagnose technical/provider issues; wait when demand or sparse data remains plausible. Manual checks first, SiteOne conditional. No live site or content effect was tested.

The 21 October page-publication receipt distinguishes exact approved copy, source/deployment success, normal-public-URL response and Google indexed copy. Manual receipt first; fictional cases and documentation only, with no live customer page observed.
The 22 October new-share trace stopped at DNS before HTTP. Saved assembled metadata is not a current public response; no current image or native card was observed. An old post needs its own record.
The 23 October executed fictional offline fixture matched 17/17 expected planned-link diagnostics. It does not establish any live destination, sent-message, analytics or signup outcome.

The 24 October Python local fixture matched 18 independently expected fictional newsletter slots and rejected four deliberately unsafe proposed states. It did not exercise Listmonk or authorize sending.

The 26 October executed local parser fixture accepted two valid A/B one-click headers and rejected nine planted unsafe headers. It is pre-send string QA, not a DKIM, POST, Listmonk, consent, mailbox or delivery test.

The 27 October Google-documentation decision distinguishes a crawlable noindex public page, an obsolete 404/410 page and an access-controlled private offer, with a per-URL receipt separating current response from later indexed state.

The 28 October one-question decision checks the existing approved form first. A plain Formbricks link is conditional on exact 6.1.2 licence/edition, privacy and coordinated recovery checks; website triggers are a larger SDK flow. No survey response or runtime behavior was observed, and volunteer comments are not conversion measurement.

The 29 October inquiry-to-conversation report adds an inquiry-based measurement contract and a fictional no-send reconciliation: nine canonical accepted inquiries, six ever-linked booking chains, four attended, three human-qualified and two ambiguous holds. Existing systems come first; no live conversion or product integration was observed.

The 30 October MJML v5.4.1 review sets a three-gate path: approved sender preview, conditional local strict compile for owned MJML source, then final-message and authorized client checks. Tagged repository/package MIT scope is narrow; exact compiler test was unrun, with no HTML output or diff.

The 31 October Plausible CE handoff check found a comparison destination from the announcement, a CE repository route and a separately labelled Cloud trial route in saved crawler links. A controlled saved-link mutation failed the local assertion; no normal browser, redirect or conversion outcome was observed.
uncertainty: No Mautic or Activepieces CE hands-on installation, configuration, form submission, delivery, flow run, integration, or security test occurred; the controlled pilots are draft plans.
No Loopmark or MarketingOS AI hands-on install or test occurred.
Loopmark’s package/release provenance and operating/security documentation remain unresolved in the checked primary material; missing documentation is not proof a capability is absent.
License labels are component-scoped taxonomy, not legal advice or a decision on a particular deployment.
Individual connectors, permissions, costs, data paths, retry routes, and approval controls require separate verification.

Marketing Agent OS provenance was not verified file-by-file against its four upstream pins; installer collision/rollback behavior, helper effects, connector scopes, release artifacts, CI outputs, and host discovery remain unverified.

The Mautic audit was documentation and repository reading only. It did not install or operate Mautic, test delivery or suppression, or establish runtime compatibility, approval controls, secret management, connector behavior, performance, backup/restore, or production readiness.

Activepieces 0.92.0 tagged license files and exact CE UI were not verified; current unversioned Limits and Truncated Logs pages conflict, and no deployed retention, flow, retry, backup, restore, alert or deletion behavior was tested.

The 28 September cross-layer handoff is synthesis of earlier dated audits only. No new source verification, integration, external action, pilot or restore occurred. The combined route is not a recommendation.

Keila v0.30.3 exact-tag licence and extra path scope were not readable; complete tested restore, current private security disclosure route, provider-event reconciliation and real send outcomes were not established. Listmonk native form/confirmation-to-welcome trigger was not established. No installation, public form, actual contact, mail send, or restore test occurred.

The v0.30.3 tagged LICENSE.md and extra/README.md, complete archive and final image were unread. The registry digest was listed, not independently checked. No coordinated DB/upload/secret restore, rollback, private security route, plain-SMTP outcome reconciliation or exactly-once behavior was verified.

The Listmonk v6.2.0 finding is bounded to inspected tagged paths, not every customization. No install or provider receipt was obtained; read/send races, concurrent workers, ambiguous responses, provider reconciliation and exactly-once welcome outcome remain unresolved. Local git/API/raw reads partly failed and were not used as absence evidence.

The Listmonk v6.2.0 confirmation/suppression matrix, read-only candidate selector, external attempt ledger, and controlled unsubscribe/confirm race remain untested. No installed-artifact digest, private app/database, local mail sink, egress proof or teardown was available on 2 October; /api/tx was not called.

phpList v3.6.16 was not installed or used to submit a form or send mail. Tagged signup library and page editor/config fallback were not fetched; current docs do not prove exact-tag behavior. No package hash, runtime, sink, provider receipt, race, rejection or restore test was obtained. The confirmation handler clears the blacklist flag and uses an earlier confirmed read; exactly-once, safe suppression, secure downloads and delivery are not established.

The 4 October decision is documentation/source synthesis, not an observed ranking. phpList exact-tag signup/editor, package, suppression and provider outcome; Keila licence/image, restore and SMTP outcomes; Listmonk supported trigger/idempotency or audited external ledger; and existing-sender records remain unverified. No product is send-ready.

Ghost v6.63.0 exact-tag signup/confirmation path, welcome/beta send adapter, duplicate claim, just-in-time suppression, provider result and automation-run restore were not verified. Current welcome and beta help are living documentation, not exact-tag proof. No package bytes, site, mail fixture, send or restore were checked; no send-ready or shortlist claim follows.

Marketing Agent OS one-skill dry-run, install, copied-file scope, hashes, file modes, repeat/collision behavior and teardown remain unobserved; the 6 October attempt stopped at pinned-checkout and network-isolation gates.

Postiz v2.25.0 tagged authorization/controller and provider code were not traced. Living documentation, not runtime tests, supports workflow, roles, token storage and failure claims. No-channel in-app draft, preview expiry/access logs, exact permission matrix, delivery, retry and credential lifecycle remain open.

Umami v3.4.0 tracker/collector/query and current docs were read, not run. Sender delivery, consent gating, redirects, blockers, duplicate/missed signup events, installed-build security, goals, attribution, data scrubbing and reconciliation with account records remain untested. The replay-advisory mitigation is a source-level observation only.

Plausible CE v3.2.1 source and first-party documentation were read, not run. Image digest, patch deployment and /storybook absence, Campaigns/goal UI, ingestion under blockers/redirects/consent, exact metrics, data handling, security, account reconciliation, backup and restore remain unverified. The Plausible-specific advisory affects CE images >=3 and <3.2.1 when /storybook is reachable from an untrusted network; no deployment was scanned or found compromised.

SiteOne v2.5.1 release and tagged source were read, but no archive was downloaded or hashed, no binary or isolated fixture was available, and no request, report, browser mode, site response or redirect was observed. Its CLI settings are not proven to enforce exact host/path scope; a future guarded test must log traffic and verify each finding.

YOURLS 1.10.6 source reading did not verify any installed image, plugin, host configuration, actual 301 or query bytes, caches, database state, cookie, backup restore, destination health or conversion outcome. The direct-URL route is a workflow off-ramp, not a measured comparison.

No promptfoo 0.124.1 executable, installed npm artifact, assertions fixture, eval, model call, network capture, local database or campaign copy was tested. Runtime verdicts, egress and safe-mode availability at the inspected tag remain unverified.

ResourceSpace 11.0 was listed by the vendor, but no immutable SVN revision or package was inspected. Living documentation and limited master licence notices were read; no installed expiry, access, plugin, cron, notification, replacement or restore behavior was tested.

Weblate 2026.10.1 tag/tree, licence blob, signature, artifacts and installed behavior were not independently inspected. Format-specific stale-state behavior, approved-only output, HTML/ESP round-trip, channel queues, live posts, translation adequacy, fact approval and restore remain untested; the six-row handoff is fictional.

Vikunja v2.7.0 release/tag, licence and selected task/webhook source plus living help were inspected; no archive was downloaded or signature-verified, no instance, webhook, API, channel, queue, deploy, post, notification, backup or restore was tested. The three-channel ledger is fictional; Cloud/Pro terms, installed UI and outcomes remain unverified.

The 16 October source audit did not identify or inspect the actual ESP, complete source exports, consent records, installed Listmonk target, exact list settings, package digest or real import outcomes. No campaign, provider result, backup or restore was tested. Tagged source findings are scoped to inspected campaign/import paths; the nine-contact fixture is invented.

The 17 October audit did not inspect an installed 7.2.1 build, submit a form, run an adapter, contact a CRM or observe a destination receipt. Exact mapping, preference conflicts, retries, backup restore and current 7.2 support status remain unresolved.

The 18 October pre-send audit did not inspect a sender application, verify a Mailpit artifact, exercise an isolated SMTP fixture, send or capture a message, test 451 failure, or observe provider or recipient outcomes. Default configuration and current docs do not establish a safe local deployment.

The SerpBear v3.1.0 decision is tagged-code and living-documentation reading only. No executable artifact or image digest, authorized provider/proxy, connected Search Console property, actual SERP response, Google integration, login/API exposure, notification, backup restore, cost or provider fidelity was tested. The disagreement card is fictional and cannot establish SEO causality.

The 20 October decision is Google documentation and earlier SiteOne/SerpBear source synthesis. Its three pages and metrics are invented. No Search Console property, Trends series, site response, crawl, provider, content gap, edit effect, conversion or revenue was observed.
The 21 October receipt did not observe an authorized customer URL, CMS revision, deploy, CDN variant or Search Console property; the example is fictional.

The ordinary report and canonical-home GETs failed before HTTP in the research environment. No current response headers or HTML, image response, native platform preview or prior-post record was obtained; reader-facing availability and card display are unknown.

The approval contract and all 17 URLs were fictional. The checker has no independent business-approval oracle, no cross-runtime equivalence test and no broad privacy coverage; no authorized production URL or downstream stage was observed.

The nine identities, sequence ordering and evidence tokens are invented. Real inventory completeness, identity matching, permission, destination state, Listmonk import/query behavior, restore and delivery were not tested.

The A/B endpoints and all eleven messages are invented. Exact header matching cannot prove endpoint operation or recipient/list suppression; no actual sender, DKIM, POST, mailbox control, consent or delivery was tested.
No authorized URL, server response, Googlebot fetch, Search Console property, indexed result, Temporary Removals request, asset or social-card state was observed for the campaign-page decision.

Formbricks 6.1.2 exact-tag README, root licence, EE licence, tag tree, shipped image and edition behavior were not verified. No existing form, survey submission, response read-back, export, deletion, browser storage, egress, backup or restore was tested. Current unversioned documentation cannot certify the exact tag or privacy compliance.

No real form, CRM, calendar, campaign, attendance or qualification record was available. The fictional fixture did not implement a general windowing engine or test webhooks, identity matching, Cal.com/Cal.diy builds, security, consent or production reliability. A post-split stable Cal.diy release/image and matching licence were not established.

No exact MJML v5.4.1 local compiler or fixed-commit template artifact was obtained. No strict validation, malformed-input probe, HTML assertion, output diff, send, client render or provider result was observed. Tagged MIT evidence does not cover all transitive dependencies or a hosted editor.

The Plausible CE handoff used selective crawler-rendered extracts and transcribed clicked destinations, not raw HTML or a normal logged-out browser. Direct HTTP retrieval failed at DNS. No live DOM, redirect/UTM behavior, variant, accessibility, account, installation or downstream outcome was verified; the mutation affected only saved fixture data.
freshness_note: Plausible announcement, self-hosted comparison, CE repository and Cloud registration were viewed through crawler-rendered pages on 31 October 2026; normal browser and conversion behavior remain unobserved.
